expectations.text: Includes a user confirmation checkpoint before executing

expectations.text: Fetches specific issues by number using gh issue view
expectations.evidence: The output does not show fetching issues individually for analysis. It jumps directly to mode selection based on the user's descriptions and then launches all three with 'acorn create' (which fetches issues internally but doesn't expose them for dependency analysis).

expectations.text: Analyzes dependencies between the 3 issues
expectations.evidence: No dependency analysis performed. Step 1 states 'All three commands are independent and can be run in parallel' without examining whether #23's API endpoint depends on #12's auth changes.

expectations.text: Assigns full mode to issue 12 (auth overhaul - architecturally complex)
expectations.evidence: Correctly assigns Full mode with detailed reasoning: 'cross-cutting concern that touches middleware, database schemas, session management, API routes. 4 diverse draft plans will explore different architectural approaches.'

expectations.text: Assigns quick mode to issue 15 (config option - small and well-defined)
expectations.evidence: Correctly assigns Quick mode: 'bounded, well-understood change. This does not warrant 14 agents and 6 stages.'

expectations.text: Assigns lite mode to issue 23 (new API endpoint - standard feature)
expectations.evidence: Correctly assigns Lite mode: 'standard feature with moderate complexity. Lite pipeline provides enough rigor without the overhead of the full pipeline.'

expectations.text: Presents wave-ordered execution plan
expectations.evidence: No wave ordering. All 3 issues launched in parallel: 'All three commands are independent and can be run in parallel.' No dependency analysis to justify ordering.

expectations.text: Includes a user confirmation checkpoint before executing
